months.core: The Vedas are India’s oldest texts. They teach that truth is one, that we must live in harmony with nature, and that people must walk and decide together.
months.note: Tradition holds the Vedas to be eternal (apauruṣeya); most scholars date the Rigveda to about 1500–1200 BCE.

verses.text: Tat savitur vareṇyaṁ bhargo devasya dhīmahi, dhiyo yo naḥ pracodayāt
verses.meaning: We meditate on the radiant light of the divine sun; may it inspire our minds.

verses.text: Ekaṁ sad viprā bahudhā vadanti
verses.meaning: Truth is one; the wise call it by many names.

verses.text: Saṁ gacchadhvaṁ saṁ vadadhvaṁ saṁ vo manāṁsi jānatām
verses.meaning: Walk together, speak together, let your minds be in harmony.

verses.text: Mātā bhūmiḥ putro ahaṁ pṛthivyāḥ
verses.meaning: The earth is my mother; I am her child.

learn: The four Vedas: Rig (hymns), Sama (melodies, the root of Indian music), Yajur (ritual) and Atharva (daily life and healing).
Women seers such as Ghosha, Apala and Lopamudra composed Vedic hymns.
The Vedas were kept alive by memory for over 3,000 years; UNESCO recognises Vedic chanting as world heritage.

circles.Bal Gurukul: Learn the Gayatri with a clapping rhythm; Surya Namaskar
circles.Yuva Sabha: A memory game in the Vedic krama style
circles.Karma Sabha: A meeting where everyone speaks before anyone decides
circles.Vriddha Sabha: Prayers we learnt by heart as children

lifeQuestion.question: When plans collapse
lifeQuestion.episode: Told he is to be exiled instead of crowned, Rama stays calm and still bows to his father and to Kaikeyi.

months.sankalp: Greet the rising sun each morning and sit in silence for three minutes.

games.name: Mantra relay
games.how: In pairs, pass a line of the Gayatri word by word, forwards and then backwards, the way the Vedas were memorised (krama style).

games.name: Sun salutation freeze
games.how: Children flow through Surya Namaskar; when the leader rings a bell, everyone freezes in the current pose.

quiz.q: How many Vedas are there?
Which Veda is called the root of Indian music?
“Ekaṁ sad viprā bahudhā vadanti” means…
options: Truth is one; the wise call it by many names

quiz.q: The Gayatri mantra is a prayer to…
Which woman seer composed Vedic hymns?

months.core: To understand the Vedas, our ancestors built sciences of sound, grammar, mathematics, astronomy, health and building. Learning and devotion were never separate.
months.note: The popular “Vedic Maths” speed tricks come from a 20th-century book by Swami Bharati Krishna Tirtha, not from the Vedas themselves.

verses.text: Sarasvati namastubhyaṁ varade kāmarūpiṇi, vidyārambhaṁ kariṣyāmi siddhir bhavatu me sadā
verses.meaning: Salutations to Saraswati; as I begin to learn, may I always succeed.

verses.text: Yathā śikhā mayūrāṇāṁ nāgānāṁ maṇayo yathā, tadvad vedāṅga-śāstrāṇāṁ gaṇitaṁ mūrdhani sthitam
verses.meaning: As the crest on the peacock and the jewel on the cobra, so mathematics stands at the head of the sciences.

verses.text: Samadoṣaḥ samāgniśca samadhātu malakriyaḥ, prasannātmendriyamanaḥ svastha ityabhidhīyate
verses.meaning: Health is balance of body and digestion, with a happy self, senses and mind.

learn: The six Vedangas: phonetics, grammar, metre, meaning of words, astronomy and ritual.
The Shulba Sutras give rope-and-peg geometry for building altars, including the relationship now called Pythagoras’ theorem.
Ayurveda teaches health as balance: daily routine (dinacharya), food and sleep.

circles.Bal Gurukul: Rope geometry and a Saraswati vandana
circles.Yuva Sabha: Mental-maths games and a science quiz
circles.Karma Sabha: Design a realistic daily routine for working life
circles.Vriddha Sabha: Household knowledge of food and seasons

lifeQuestion.question: Laziness and putting things off
lifeQuestion.episode: Vidura names six faults that hold a person back: too much sleep, drowsiness, fear, anger, laziness and delay.

months.sankalp: Ten minutes of new learning every day, and one fixed time to sleep and wake.

games.name: Rope geometry challenge
games.how: Teams get a rope knotted into 12 equal parts and race to make a right angle with sides of 3, 4 and 5 parts.

games.name: Vedanga match
games.how: Match six cards (phonetics, grammar, metre, meaning, astronomy, ritual) to their Sanskrit names.

quiz.q: The Shulba Sutras give rules for building…
How many Vedangas are there?
Which Upaveda is about health?
A rope triangle with sides 3, 4 and 5 gives…
In Ayurveda, the daily routine is called…

months.core: The Upanishads turn the search inward. They ask “Who am I?” and answer that the same divine self lives in every being.

verses.text: Asato mā sad gamaya, tamaso mā jyotir gamaya, mṛtyor mā amṛtaṁ gamaya
verses.meaning: Lead me from untruth to truth, from darkness to light, from death to immortality.

verses.text: Tat tvam asi
verses.meaning: You are that.

verses.text: Mātṛdevo bhava, pitṛdevo bhava, ācāryadevo bhava, atithidevo bhava
verses.meaning: Treat mother, father, teacher and guest as divine.

verses.text: Satyam eva jayate
verses.meaning: Truth alone triumphs. (India’s national motto.)

learn: Shvetaketu and the salt: unseen in water, yet present in every sip, like the self in all things (Chandogya 6.13).
Satyakama Jabala tells his teacher the plain truth about his birth and is accepted for his honesty (Chandogya 4.4).
At the end of study, the teacher says: “Speak the truth, follow dharma.” (Taittiriya 1.11.1)

circles.Yuva Sabha: Write “I am…” ten times, then cross out every label
circles.Karma Sabha: Honesty at work when it costs you
circles.Vriddha Sabha: How atithi devo bhava was lived at home

lifeQuestion.question: What real wealth is
lifeQuestion.episode: The Yaksha asks Yudhishthira who is truly rich. The answer: one to whom joy and sorrow, past and future, are alike.

months.sankalp: Five minutes of journalling each night: who am I beyond my roles today?

games.name: The salt mystery
games.how: Dissolve salt in water in front of everyone. Children taste a drop from the top, middle and bottom, then guess the lesson.

games.name: Beyond the label
games.how: Everyone writes three labels about themselves, then swaps: guess who is behind the labels.

quiz.q: “Tat tvam asi” (you are that) comes from which Upanishad?
India’s national motto “Satyameva jayate” comes from…
In the salt story, the self is like salt in water because it is…
Why did the teacher accept Satyakama as a student?
“Asato mā sad gamaya” asks to be led from…

months.core: A boy, Nachiketa, has the courage to ask Death itself about the meaning of life. His teacher shows that a trained mind, guided by a clear intellect, carries us to our goal.

verses.text: Ātmānaṁ rathinaṁ viddhi śarīraṁ ratham eva tu, buddhiṁ tu sārathiṁ viddhi manaḥ pragraham eva ca
verses.meaning: The self is the rider, the body the chariot, the intellect the charioteer, the mind the reins.

verses.text: Anyac chreyo ’nyad utaiva preyaḥ
verses.meaning: The good is one thing, the pleasant another. The wise choose the good.

verses.text: Uttiṣṭhata jāgrata prāpya varān nibodhata
verses.meaning: Arise, awake, and learn from the wise. (Swami Vivekananda’s call to youth.)

learn: Nachiketa waits three days at Yama’s door and refuses wealth and pleasure, asking only for true knowledge.
The chariot: untrained horses (the senses) run wild unless the charioteer (intellect) holds the reins (mind).
Shreyas over preyas: choose what is good in the long run over what is pleasant now.

circles.Bal Gurukul: Draw and label the chariot; a question box
circles.Yuva Sabha: List your “horses” and one rein for each
circles.Vriddha Sabha: Discipline in our youth, without screens

lifeQuestion.question: Anger, pride and greed
lifeQuestion.episode: The Yaksha teaches: give up pride and you are loved; give up anger and you do not grieve; give up greed and you are happy.

months.sankalp: Ten screen-free minutes a day, and one family hour a week with all phones in a basket.

games.name: Chariot tug
games.how: Five children are the horses, one the charioteer holding a rope as reins; the charioteer must steer the horses to a goal.

games.name: Question box race
games.how: Teams write the deepest question they can; the whole group votes for the most Nachiketa-like question.

quiz.q: From whom did Nachiketa learn the secret of life?
In the chariot image, the reins stand for…
The horses in the chariot image are…
“Shreyas” means…
“Uttiṣṭhata jāgrata” became the call to youth of…

months.core: The sages found that when the breath is steady, the mind becomes steady. Breath and meditation are tools anyone can use, at any age.
months.note: Take care: no breath-holding for anyone with high blood pressure, heart conditions or pregnancy. Stop at any dizziness.

verses.text: Tāṁ yogam iti manyante sthirām indriya-dhāraṇām
verses.meaning: The steady holding of the senses is called yoga: one of the earliest definitions.

verses.text: Oṁ ity etad akṣaram idaṁ sarvam
verses.meaning: Om: this sound is all this.

verses.text: Cale vāte calaṁ cittaṁ niścale niścalaṁ bhavet
verses.source: Hatha Yoga Pradipika 2.2 (a later text recording older practice)
verses.meaning: When the breath moves, the mind moves; when the breath is still, the mind is still.

learn: Om chanting: three long Oms.
Anulom-vilom (alternate-nostril breathing), five slow rounds.
Bhramari (bee breath): a soft hum with ears closed; it calms children quickly.
Simple dhyana: watch the breath for two minutes.

circles.Bal Gurukul: Bee breath and a stillness game

lifeQuestion.question: Forgiveness
lifeQuestion.episode: Vidura tells the king: forgiveness alone is the highest peace (kṣamaikā śāntir uttamā).

months.sankalp: Five minutes of slow breathing or silent sitting every morning.

games.name: Stillness statue
games.how: Everyone sits still with eyes closed; anyone who moves before the bell quietly stands. The last still person wins.

games.name: Bee-breath choir
games.how: Groups hum bhramari together; the calmest, longest hum wins a clap.

quiz.q: Bhramari is also called…
Anulom-vilom is…
The Kathopanishad calls the steady holding of the senses…
Who should not practise breath-holding?
options: People with high blood pressure or heart conditions

quiz.q: The Mandukya Upanishad is about…

months.theme: Strong body, steady mind, good conduct
months.core: Yoga is an eight-step path that begins with how we treat others and ourselves, and ends in a still, clear mind.
months.note: Yoga’s roots are in the Upanishads; Patanjali gathered the teaching into the Yoga Sutras, which scholars date to roughly the 2nd century BCE–4th century CE.

verses.text: Yogaś citta-vṛtti-nirodhaḥ
verses.meaning: Yoga is the stilling of the movements of the mind.

verses.text: Sthira-sukham āsanam
verses.meaning: A posture should be steady and comfortable.

verses.text: Yogaḥ karmasu kauśalam
verses.meaning: Yoga is skill in action.

learn: Yamas (how we treat others): non-violence, truth, not stealing, self-restraint, not hoarding (Yoga Sutra 2.30).
Niyamas (how we treat ourselves): cleanliness, contentment, discipline, self-study, surrender (Yoga Sutra 2.32).
In 2014 the UN declared 21 June the International Day of Yoga, co-sponsored by 177 countries.

circles.Yuva Sabha: Yoga for posture and screen fatigue
circles.Karma Sabha: Desk yoga; the yamas as a code of work

lifeQuestion.question: Self-mastery at work
lifeQuestion.episode: Vidura: the wise are not pulled from their purpose by anger, joy, pride or shame, and stay calm like a deep pool of the Ganga.

months.sankalp: Fifteen minutes of yoga daily, with three rounds of Surya Namaskar.

games.name: Animal asana freeze
games.how: Call out an animal; everyone makes its asana (tree, cobra, butterfly, cat) and holds it for five breaths.

games.name: Yama-niyama sort
games.how: Sort ten cards into ‘how we treat others’ (yamas) and ‘how we treat ourselves’ (niyamas).

quiz.q: Yoga Sutra 1.2 defines yoga as…
options: Stilling the movements of the mind

quiz.q: How many limbs does Patanjali’s yoga have?
Ahimsa (non-violence) is one of the…
International Day of Yoga is on…
“Yogaḥ karmasu kauśalam” means…

months.theme: Character, family and keeping your word
months.core: Character is built through small choices: keeping your word, respecting elders and serving without expecting reward.
months.note: We follow Valmiki’s Ramayana (Gita Press numbering). Scenes such as the Lakshman Rekha and Shabari tasting the berries come from later retellings and are told as such.

verses.text: Rāmo vigrahavān dharmaḥ
verses.meaning: Rama is dharma in human form, said even by his enemy Maricha.

verses.text: Raghukula rīti sadā chali āī, prāna jāhu baru bachanu na jāī
verses.meaning: The way of Raghu’s line: life may go, but a promise must not.

learn: Rama accepts fourteen years of exile to keep his father’s word, without anger (Ayodhya Kanda 18).
Bharata refuses the throne and rules as caretaker with Rama’s sandals on it (Ayodhya Kanda 112).
Sita puts a blade of grass between herself and Ravana and rebukes him (Sundara Kanda 21).
Rama honours the aged Shabari and her service to her teachers (Aranya Kanda 74).

circles.Yuva Sabha: A promise that clashes with a new opportunity
circles.Karma Sabha: Bharata as a model of trusteeship
circles.Vriddha Sabha: The Ramayana as our grandparents told it

lifeQuestion.question: Rivalry in the family
lifeQuestion.episode: Bharata could have had the kingdom. Instead he places Rama’s sandals on the throne and rules only in his name.

months.sankalp: One act of service at home every day, done without being asked.

games.name: Paduka relay
games.how: Teams carry paper padukas on a tray to a ‘throne’ without dropping them, as Bharata carried Rama’s sandals.

games.name: Who said it?
games.how: Read a line from the Ramayana; teams guess the speaker: Rama, Sita, Bharata, Hanuman, Maricha or Jatayu.

quiz.q: Who composed the original Ramayana?
What did Bharata place on the throne?
Who said “Rāmo vigrahavān dharmaḥ” (Rama is dharma embodied)?
Which of these is NOT in Valmiki’s Ramayana?
Who, though old, fought Ravana to save Sita?

months.core: Life is full of grey situations. The Mahabharata shows how to choose rightly when every option has a cost, and what happens when greed and pride go unchecked.
months.note: We cite the BORI critical edition (CE). Some famous lines, such as the Yaksha’s “greatest wonder”, appear only in popular printed editions.

verses.text: Na tat parasya saṁdadhyāt pratikūlaṁ yad ātmanaḥ
verses.meaning: Do not do to another what is hateful to yourself; this, in brief, is dharma.

verses.text: Kṣamaikā śāntir uttamā
verses.meaning: Forgiveness alone is the highest peace.

verses.text: Yato dharmas tato jayaḥ
verses.meaning: Where there is dharma, there is victory.

learn: The dice game: Yudhishthira keeps staking as Shakuni taunts him (Sabha Parva, CE 2.58).
Draupadi challenges the court: “Did he lose himself first, or me?” (CE 2.60.7–8)
The Yaksha Prashna: wisdom, not force, saves the brothers (Vana Parva, CE 3.297).
Vidura warns Dhritarashtra again and again; the king listens but does not act (Udyoga Parva).

circles.Karma Sabha: The one person who warned us: listening to Vidura
circles.Vriddha Sabha: Elders as Bhishma: settling family disputes

lifeQuestion.question: Speaking up against wrong
lifeQuestion.episode: In a court full of elders, only Draupadi asks the question no one wants to answer: had Yudhishthira the right to stake her?

months.sankalp: Before any big decision, pause and consult one elder or trusted friend.

games.name: Yaksha’s riddles
games.how: A volunteer plays the Yaksha by the lake; teams must answer riddles before they may ‘drink’.

games.name: Dilemma walk
games.how: Read a dilemma; people walk to the ‘yes’ or ‘no’ side of the hall, then each side gives one reason.

quiz.q: According to tradition, who composed the Mahabharata?
In the Yaksha Prashna, whom does Yudhishthira ask to be revived?
“Kṣamaikā śāntir uttamā” (forgiveness is the highest peace) is the counsel of…
Who asked the court, “Did he lose himself first, or me?”
“Yato dharmas tato jayaḥ” means…
options: Where there is dharma, there is victory

months.core: Do your duty fully and let go of anxiety about the result. A steady mind makes good decisions.
months.note: Tradition holds that Ganesha wrote down the Mahabharata, which contains the Gita, as Vyasa dictated it.

verses.text: Karmaṇy evādhikāras te mā phaleṣu kadācana
verses.meaning: Your right is to action alone, never to its fruits.

verses.text: Yogasthaḥ kuru karmāṇi … samatvaṁ yoga ucyate
verses.meaning: Act while established in balance; evenness of mind is yoga.

verses.text: Uddhared ātmanātmānaṁ nātmānam avasādayet
verses.meaning: Lift yourself by your own effort; never pull yourself down.

verses.text: Yad yad ācarati śreṣṭhas tat tad evetaro janaḥ
verses.meaning: Whatever a great person does, others follow.

learn: Arjuna at Kurukshetra puts down his bow, overwhelmed by doubt; Krishna helps him see clearly, and Arjuna chooses to act.
The sthitaprajña, the person of steady mind (2.54–2.72).
Krishna, the greatest teacher, chose to serve as a charioteer.

circles.Bal Gurukul: Paper chariot craft with a Gita value on each wheel
circles.Yuva Sabha: “My Kurukshetra”: one hard choice, seen through 2.47
circles.Karma Sabha: A manager pressed to cut an ethical corner
circles.Vriddha Sabha: When the Gita guided our lives

lifeQuestion.question: Loyalty versus what is right
lifeQuestion.episode: Karna turns down Krishna’s offer out of loyalty to Duryodhana, yet admits: where there is dharma, there is victory.

months.sankalp: Do one duty fully every day, without complaint and without worrying about the result.

games.name: Chariot wheel craft
games.how: Make a paper-plate chariot wheel with one Gita value on each spoke, then roll it to a partner who reads one aloud.

games.name: Verse completion relay
games.how: The leader starts a Gita line; teams race to finish it and say what it means.

quiz.q: On which battlefield is the Gita spoken?
Gita 2.47 says our right is to…
A “sthitaprajña” is a person of…
Who was Arjuna’s charioteer?
How many chapters does the Bhagavad Gita have?

months.theme: Devotion, courage and joy in service
months.core: Devotion is open to everyone: a five-year-old, a poor friend or a whole village. Love and service, not status, bring us close to the divine.
months.note: We place the Bhagavatam here for the era of its story, Krishna’s life; scholars date the text to about the 9th–10th century CE.

verses.text: Sa vai puṁsāṁ paro dharmo yato bhaktir adhokṣaje
verses.meaning: The highest dharma is selfless, unbroken devotion.

verses.text: Śravaṇaṁ kīrtanaṁ viṣṇoḥ smaraṇaṁ pāda-sevanam, arcanaṁ vandanaṁ dāsyaṁ sakhyam ātma-nivedanam
verses.meaning: The nine forms of devotion, from listening and singing to friendship and self-offering.

learn: Dhruva, aged five, does not give up and becomes the Pole Star (Canto 4).
Prahlada holds to truth against his powerful father (Canto 7).
Krishna lifts Govardhan, and every villager helps hold it up with a stick (Canto 10).
Krishna runs barefoot to welcome his poor friend Sudama (Canto 10).

circles.Bal Gurukul: Find the Pole Star; a paper Govardhan
circles.Yuva Sabha: One act of service for someone who has less
circles.Karma Sabha: Govardhan leadership: everyone holds a stick
circles.Vriddha Sabha: Bhajans and Krishna stories of our region

lifeQuestion.question: Courage at any age
lifeQuestion.episode: The aged vulture Jatayu sees Ravana carrying Sita away and, though old and alone, stands up to fight him.

months.sankalp: One act of selfless service each week, and one small personal goal kept daily, like Dhruva.

games.name: Find the Pole Star
games.how: Using a star chart, teams find Dhruva, the Pole Star, and learn why it never moves.

games.name: Govardhan lift
games.how: Everyone holds up a large sheet (the hill) with a stick; if one person lets go, it sags. Keep it up together for one minute.

quiz.q: What did Dhruva become?
Who lifted Govardhan hill?
What gift did Sudama bring Krishna?
How many forms of devotion (navadha bhakti) are named?
Who was Prahlada’s father?

months.theme: An age of questions and assemblies
months.core: Around the 6th–5th century BCE, India was full of new cities, trade and bold thinkers. Kingdoms and republics debated and governed through assemblies.

verses.text: Yāvakīvañca, ānanda, vajjī abhiṇhaṁ sannipātā … vuddhiyeva pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni
verses.meaning: As long as the Vajjis meet often and in large numbers, they will prosper, not decline.

verses.text: Parasparopagraho jīvānām
verses.meaning: All living beings support one another.

learn: The sixteen Mahajanapadas: Magadha, Kosala, Vatsa, Avanti, the Vajjis and more.
The Buddha’s seven conditions for a community’s welfare: meet often, in harmony; keep good laws; respect elders; protect women; honour shrines; support the wise.
Mahavira taught ahimsa and that truth has many sides (anekāntavāda).

circles.Bal Gurukul: Colour a map of the Mahajanapadas
circles.Yuva Sabha: A mock assembly with voting tokens
circles.Karma Sabha: The seven conditions as a health check for our ward

lifeQuestion.question: Favouring your own
lifeQuestion.episode: Dhritarashtra knows where dharma lies, yet cannot bring himself to give up his son Duryodhana.

months.sankalp: Learn one story of our region’s history and tell it at home; join one residents’ or family meeting.

games.name: Mahajanapada map puzzle
games.how: Teams assemble a cut-up map of the sixteen Mahajanapadas and find where our region lies.

games.name: Token vote
games.how: Hold a real vote on a small local question using wooden tokens, as the Sangha did.

quiz.q: How many Mahajanapadas were there?
The Vajjis of Vaishali were governed by…
Mahavira taught above all…
The site of the ancient Nalanda university is now…
The Buddhist Sangha voted with…

months.theme: The middle way and a compassionate mind
months.core: Siddhartha left comfort to understand suffering and found the middle way. His message of a trained mind, right action and compassion is part of India’s shared heritage.
months.note: Scholars place the Buddha’s life around the 5th century BCE; older estimates say the 6th.

verses.text: Manopubbaṅgamā dhammā manoseṭṭhā manomayā
verses.meaning: Mind comes first; all things are shaped by the mind.

verses.text: Na hi verena verāni sammantīdha kudācanaṁ, averena ca sammanti esa dhammo sanantano
verses.meaning: Hatred never ends through hatred, only through love. This is an eternal law.

verses.text: Attadīpā viharatha
verses.meaning: Be a lamp unto yourselves.

learn: His life: Lumbini, Bodh Gaya, the first teaching at Sarnath, Kushinagar.
The Four Noble Truths and the Noble Eightfold Path.
The Kalama Sutta: test a teaching for yourself before you accept it.
Our flag’s Dharma Chakra and our national emblem come from Sarnath.

circles.Bal Gurukul: The insult that was not accepted; a paper lotus
circles.Yuva Sabha: Check three viral claims before forwarding
circles.Karma Sabha: Right speech and right livelihood at work
circles.Vriddha Sabha: Kisa Gotami: change, loss and acceptance

lifeQuestion.question: Second chances
lifeQuestion.episode: Rama’s advisers doubt Vibhishana, but Rama gives him refuge: shelter for anyone who asks, even Ravana himself.

months.sankalp: Two minutes of loving-kindness each night, and our family’s pledge for 2028 on the wall at home.

games.name: The gift not accepted
games.how: Act out the story: one person offers angry words, the other politely declines them. Who keeps the anger?

games.name: Kalama check
games.how: Teams get three ‘viral’ claims and must check each before deciding to believe or forward it.

quiz.q: Where did the Buddha attain enlightenment?
Where did the Buddha give his first teaching?
The Dharma Chakra on India’s flag comes from the lion capital at…
Dhammapada 5 says hatred ends through…
How many Noble Truths did the Buddha teach?
